newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares weaken with Volvo adding pressure.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares weaken with Volvo adding pressure.

text.p: Sweden's stockmarket was weaker by midday Wednesday in fairly light trade with vehicle maker Volvo partly to blame for weighing down the market.
The Stockholm bourse was 0.41 percent lower at 2156.49 after shares worth 1.2 billion crowns changed hands.
"It seems as if the market is having a pause (after recent record highs)," one broker said. "We will see if anything happens when the U.S. opens."
Volvo was the focus in morning trade, reporting a slightly disappointing result for the first nine months of 1996.
Volvo shares slipped four crowns to 137.
Bluechip stocks were mixed. Telecoms giant Ericsson was 1.5 lower at 181.50 crowns while drugs major Astra rose 1.5 to 308 crowns.
The forestry sector was the best performing industry in morning trade with the index up 0.53 percent. Stora was steady at 86.50 crowns while MoDo slipped one to 181 crowns.
